t:
(a) Authorization of Appropriations.—Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal years beginning after September 30, 2006, for military construction, land acquisition, and military family housing functions of the Department of the Air Force in the total amount of $3,231,442,000, as follows:
        (1) For military construction projects inside the United States authorized by section 2301(a), $962,286,000. 
        (2) For military construction projects outside the United States authorized by section 2301(b), $157,966,000. 
        (3) For military construction projects at unspecified worldwide locations authorized by section 2301(c), $9,677,000. 
        (4) For unspecified minor military construction projects authorized by section 2805 of title 10, United States Code, $15,000,000. 
        (5) For architectural and engineering services and construction design under section 2807 of title 10, United States Code, $79,004,000. 
        (6) For military family housing functions:
            (A) For construction and acquisition, planning and design, and improvement of military family housing and facilities, $1,168,138,000. 
            (B) For support of military family housing (including functions described in section 2833 of title 10, United States Code), $755,071,000.  
        (7) For the construction of increment 2 of the C–17 maintenance complex at Elmendorf Air Force Base, Alaska, authorized by section 2301(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (division B of Public Law 109–163; 119 Stat. 3494), $30,000,000. 
        (8) For the construction of increment 2 of the main base runway at Edwards Air Force Base, California, authorized by section 2301(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (division B of Public Law 109–163; 119 Stat. 3494), $31,000,000. 
        (9) For the construction of increment 2 of the CENTCOM Joint Intelligence Center at MacDill Air Force Base, Florida, authorized by section 2301(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (division B of Public Law 109–163; 119 Stat. 3494), as amended by section 2305 of this Act, $23,300,000.  
    (b) Limitation on Total Cost of Construction Projects.—Notwithstanding the cost variations authorized by section 2853 of title 10, United States Code, and any other cost variation authorized by law, the total cost of all projects carried out under section 2301 of this Act may not exceed the total amount authorized to be appropriated under paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subsection (a).

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations for Air Force military construction and family housing and caps total project costs. There is no tempting reading here: it contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, right to sue, or consultation with states, tribes, or any other party outside the federal government. Every actor involved is inside the federal government, so it is not participation.
fable.s: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal years beginning after September 30, 2006, for military construction, land acquisition, and military family housing functions of the Department of the Air Force

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations authorization that allocates specific dollar amounts for military construction and housing projects. It does not contain any language requiring consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making decisions. The text focuses solely on funding levels and cost limitations for internal Department of Defense activities.
qwen_block.s: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal years beginning after September 30, 2006, for military construction, land acquisition, and military family housing functions of the Department of the Air Force in the total amount of $3,231,442,000

opus.w: This section only authorizes funding for Air Force military construction and family housing, and caps the total cost of the projects. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue. Mentions of 'architectural and engineering services' or 'design' might seem to involve outside parties, but they are just categories of spending, not a role in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is purely an authorization of appropriations for military construction and housing. It lists specific dollar amounts for various projects but does not require any consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties. All entities involved in the decision-making described here (the Department of the Air Force, Congress) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal years beginning after September 30, 2006, for military construction, land acquisition, and military family housing functions of the Department of the Air Force in the total amount of $3,231,442,000
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for military construction, there could be implicit public hearings or environmental reviews required by other laws (like NEPA). However, this specific section only authorizes appropriations and sets cost limits. It does not explicitly mandate any consultation, comment period, or participation process within its own text. The actors mentioned are the Department of the Air Force and Congress (via the authorization), all of whom are inside the federal government.
